profile.reading:
Tahoe Reno 2 is one of the named future buildings on Switch's "Citadel Campus" in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, Nevada, adjacent to the Tesla Gigafactory. Switch's only public reference specifically naming Tahoe Reno 2 is a November 19, 2020 press release announcing that construction had been "accelerated" on the building, alongside site preparation beginning on the neighboring Tahoe Reno 3; that release did not give individual square footage, megawatt, or completion-date figures for either building, describing the full future campus build-out only in aggregate as "more than 7 million square feet and over 600 megawatts." Switch's FY2021 SEC 10-K filing, covering the period through December 31, 2021, lists the Citadel Campus portfolio as one current facility (Tahoe Reno 1) plus seven future facilities totaling 5.89 million gross square feet and 520 megawatts combined, without breaking that total out by individual building, meaning that as of Switch's last public-company financial disclosure, Tahoe Reno 2 had not yet opened and had no individually reported specifications. This OSM record shares the same 1 Superloop Circle address as Tahoe Reno 1 and the other numbered Tahoe Reno buildings in this dataset, consistent with all being part of one large campus rather than having individually distinct street addresses. Switch's current marketing describes the full Citadel Campus at up to 17.4 million square feet and more than 2 gigawatts of power at completion, a scale increase from the 2020-2021 figures reflecting continued campus expansion since Switch's 2022 acquisition by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors.

Storey County's Tahoe Reno Industrial Center spans roughly 107,000 acres and hosts more than 100 tenants beyond Switch, including Tesla's Gigafactory and Google, drawing more than 900 megawatts of on-site power generation capacity across the broader industrial park. Switch's 2020 press release describing accelerated construction on Tahoe Reno 2 specifically cited "multi-megawatt expansions with global e-commerce and semiconductor clients" as the demand driver behind the acceleration, tying this building's development timeline to named customer categories even though Switch has not disclosed which specific tenants occupy or are contracted for the building.

sources.title: Switch Press Release, Tahoe Reno 2 and 3 Construction Update

profile.capacity_note: Up to 7.2 million sq ft and up to 650 MW is the Citadel Campus full build-out target across many more buildings than the five this registry tracks, per the operators own press release, not a single-building figure, so not applied to critical_it_mw.
profile.research_note: Switch has never individually specified Tahoe Reno 2's capacity or square footage; only the FY2021 10-K's aggregate 520MW/5.89M sqft across "seven future facilities" is public, not broken out per building. No per-building MW/sqft is asserted for this row.

reading.body:
This facility is part of Switch's Citadel Campus in Storey County, Nevada, a 2,000-acre site adjacent to the Tesla Gigafactory designed for up to 7.2 million square feet and 650 MW at full build-out, though the operator has not published how much of that capacity exists today or how much power this specific building, Tahoe Reno 2, consumes. The registry maps 26 facilities across Nevada, but only two operators publish power figures, making Tahoe Reno 2 the third-largest disclosed capacity in the state by the operator's claimed eventual scale relative to what has been measured elsewhere in Nevada.

The campus location in Storey County places it in the same industrial corridor as major manufacturing and energy infrastructure, but the operator's own locations page confirms no street address and directs inquiries to a contact form, so the precise power availability, transmission connection, water supply, and current operational status of Tahoe Reno 2 are not published. The full-build-out target of 650 MW across multiple buildings vastly exceeds the total of 10.37 MW published by all operators in Nevada combined, but this figure applies to the entire Citadel Campus, not to this single facility.

Without published megawatt figures for Tahoe Reno 2 itself, its relevance to AI scaling cannot be calculated from specifications alone. If the facility were operating at 100 MW of IT load, a conservative estimate for a single exascale building, it would at 40 kW per rack contain roughly 2,500 racks, but this is an assumption not confirmed by the operator. The campus's announced 650 MW target suggests significant planned capacity for compute, yet the absence of current power draw or completion timelines means Tahoe Reno 2's actual contribution to grid-constrained AI deployment remains unknown.
